description: Hand-curated catalog of every reusable object prefab in the Piccolo asset library. Read by the Python agent harness to construct legal object-instance requests without hallucinating field names or component paths. The engine itself never reads this file.
units: meters and seconds; positions are (x, y, z) with y up
coordinate_note: Piccolo uses a Z-up world for the character controller (jump raises z), but levels also set y. The verifier reads the actual runtime position from get_state and checks whichever axis the MotorComponent treats as vertical. Prefer z for jump assertions.

assets.description: Third-person player character: physics capsule body, humanoid skeleton animation, skinned mesh, motor controller (move/jump/sprint), and a follow camera. A Lua script tweaks jump height based on movement state.

collision.note: half-height is the cylindrical portion, excluding caps

MotorComponent.m_jump_height.desc: Jump apex height (overridden by Lua script at runtime)

assets.notes: Exactly one Player per level is required for camera-follow and motor-driven movement. Place at a position clear of other colliders so the capsule does not spawn inside a wall.

assets.description: A plain static wall, thin in x and tall in y, oriented along z. Good for enclosing an arena or blocking line of sight.

collision.note: full size 0.3 x 10.0 x 7.0; local position offset z=3.5

TransformComponent.m_position.desc: World placement of the wall's local origin

assets.notes: Rotate about y to orient the long axis. Multiple instances tile along z to form long barriers.

assets.description: A solid cube block, 2x2x2 meters. The simplest collidable prop; stackable to build simple structures.

collision.note: full size 2.0 x 2.0 x 2.0; local position offset z=1.0

TransformComponent.m_position.desc: World placement of the block's local origin

assets.notes: Useful as an obstacle the player must jump over or walk around.

assets.description: A wall section with a window opening — same footprint as wall, but the middle is hollow so the player can see (not walk) through.

collision.note: multiple box shapes leave a window gap in the center

assets.notes: Collision is solid except for the window opening; the character capsule is too tall to pass through.

assets.description: A wall section with a door opening — the gap is tall enough for the character capsule to walk through.

collision.note: boxes flanking a central doorway gap

assets.notes: Use to create passages and rooms the player can actually traverse.

assets.description: A low decorative fence. Multiple box shapes form a perimeter; shorter than the wall.

collision.note: four box shapes enclosing a rectangular area

assets.notes: Treat as a boundary marker; jumping over it may be possible depending on height.

assets.description: A short flight of stepped boxes rising in height. Lets the character walk up to a higher elevation.

collision.note: seven stacked boxes of increasing height form the steps

TransformComponent.m_position.desc: World placement of the step stack

assets.notes: Character controller sweep may or may not climb these cleanly; use for elevation tests, not as a hard barrier.

assets.description: A large flat ground plane. Place exactly one to give the level a walkable surface and prevent the character from falling forever.

collision.note: very large flat slab; acts as the ground

TransformComponent.m_position.desc: World placement; keep y low so the top surface is the ground plane

assets.notes: Essential for any playable scene — without it the character capsule has nothing to rest on. One per level is usually enough.

assets.description: A GPU particle emitter. Visual only — no collision and no gameplay interaction.

TransformComponent.m_position.desc: Where the emitter sits in the world

assets.notes: Decorative. The verifier ignores particle objects entirely; do not rely on them for gameplay.
